pumac-2018-algebra-a-07.prompt: Let the sequence $\{a_n\}_{n=-2}^{\infty}$ satisfy $a_{-1}=a_{-2}=0$, $a_0=1$, and for all non-negative integers $n$, $$n^2=\sum_{k=0}^{n}a_{n-k}a_{k-1}+\sum_{k=0}^{n}a_{n-k}a_{k-2}.$$ Given $a_{2018}$ is rational, find the maximum integer $m$ such that $2^m$ divides the denominator of the reduced form of $a_{2018}$.

pumac-2018-algebra-a-08.prompt: $$\frac pq=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{2^{n+6}}\cdot\frac{\left(10-4\cos^2(2n)\right)\left(1-(-1)^n\right)-3\cos(2n)\left(1+(-1)^n\right)}{25-16\cos^2(2n)}$$ where $p$ and $q$ are relatively prime positive integers. Find $p+q$.
pumac-2018-algebra-a-08.reviewNote: The printed paper has cos(pi n/24) in the summand; with that angle the sum is pi/24 (irrational), so no p/q exists. The official solution and key (97) use cos(2n); the prompt is stored with cos(2n).
